title: Donor building owner
intro: The donor building owner holds buildings that are coming down or being stripped out, and decides what in them is recovered, who may see it and who may reserve it. They appoint the surveyor and the deconstruction contractor, ask testing companies for tests, track the requirements that apply before demolition, list lots privately, in confidence or publicly, and answer reservation requests. Every owner can also read the Marketplace, and can be the client of its own New project, sourcing reclaimed materials with an architect.

workflows.title: Add a donor building
workflows.where: Buildings (/app/buildings), button Add building, or Add building in the sidebar under Donor buildings (/app/buildings?new=1)
workflows.summary: The owner records a building that is coming down or being stripped out, so it can be surveyed and what it holds offered for reuse. The record is private to the owner organisation; nothing is listed until the owner decides.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Buildings, press Add building"]:::owner --> B["Choose Donor building"]:::owner
B --> C["Enter name, address, region and local authority"]:::owner
C --> D["Add optional facts, structure, programme"]:::owner
D --> E{"Details valid?"}:::system
E -->|"No"| F(["Error shown, fix and retry"]):::system
E -->|"Yes"| G["Building saved as private"]:::system
G --> R["Requirements before demolition tracked"]:::system
R --> H{"Surveyor chosen?"}:::owner
H -->|"Yes"| I["Surveyor told they are appointed"]:::system
H -->|"No"| J(["Appoint a surveyor later"]):::owner
I --> K(["Building ready for capture"]):::surveyor

steps.action: Presses Add building and, under What kind of building?, picks Donor building.

Enters the building name and address and chooses the Region (required), and optionally the postcode district and the Local authority. The local authority list holds every listed authority grouped by region, so choosing one also sets the region; outside London, Another local authority takes a typed name.
Optionally adds the year built, storeys, floor area, the structure element by element, and the programme dates: Strip-out starts, Dismantling starts, Site clear by.
Optionally picks a firm under Surveyor, then presses Add donor building.

Checks the details, saves the building as private with location shown by region and timing by three-month window, starts tracking the requirements that apply before demolition at that place, and opens its Overview.
If a surveyor was chosen, tells that firm it is appointed and links it to Capture.

Can later change the name, address, postcode district, region, local authority and programme with Edit details on the building, and the structure on the Overview. A move says how many requirements before demolition stop applying and how many more are tracked.

rules: Only a donor building owner can add a donor building this way.
Name, address and region are required. The year built must be between 1800 and this year.

A listed local authority is accepted only under its own region: "Choose a local authority in this region." A typed name that is in fact listed says where it is listed. A typed name is accepted only outside London. Names are stored in their listed spelling, so "westminster" or "Westminster City Council" both read Westminster.
The programme dates must run in order: strip-out, then dismantling, then clear by. Otherwise the save is refused.
The surveyor, if chosen, must be a surveying or deconstruction firm.
The building and everything captured in it stay private to the owner and the firms working on it until the owner lists something.
notifications: The chosen surveying firm: "[owner] appointed you to survey [building]", linking to Capture.
The building activity log records that the owner added it.

workflows.title: Add a new project and appoint an architect
workflows.where: Add new project on Buildings (/app/buildings?new=project), in the New projects section of the owner Home, or on the Marketplace strip Building something too?; or Add building, then New project. The project opens at /app/projects/:id
workflows.summary: A New project is a building the owner is putting up or refurbishing. The owner organisation becomes its client and developer, and appoints an architecture practice who shortlists reclaimed materials; the owner then approves and reserves them, as any client would.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Press Add new project"]:::owner --> B["Dialog opens on New project"]:::system
B --> C["Enter name, type, region, RIBA stage"]:::owner
C --> D["Set date materials needed on site"]:::owner
D --> E{"Details valid?"}:::system
E -->|"No"| F(["Error shown, fix and retry"]):::system
E -->|"Yes"| G["Project created, owner is client"]:::system
G --> H{"Architect chosen?"}:::owner
H -->|"No"| J["Owner may keep or edit the dates"]:::owner
J --> P["Appoint an architect later"]:::owner
H -->|"Yes"| I["Architect told, shortlist ready"]:::system
P --> I
I --> K["Architect shortlists materials"]:::arch
K --> L(["Owner approves and reserves"]):::owner

steps.action: Presses Add new project on Buildings or on the owner Home, which opens the dialog on New project with Project name; or presses Add building and picks New project.
Enters the project name, region, project type and RIBA stage, and optionally the local authority from the grouped list. If the type is Other, a short description for the team only.
Sets Materials needed on site from; the stage dates are suggested from it.
Optionally picks an Architect, then presses Add new project.
Creates the project with the owner organisation as client, already linked, adds a New projects section to the owner sidebar and shows a quiet New project pill in the project header for the owner.
If an architect was chosen, adds them to the team, opens their shortlist for the project and tells them.
While no architect is appointed, may press Keep these dates or Edit programme on the project's programme card to set the dates itself.
If no architect was chosen, uses the card Appoint an architect to start sourcing on the project Overview or Team tab, or Appoint on the Buildings list, and presses Appoint.
On appointment, dates the owner set read "Client's dates" for the architect, who keeps or edits them; the owner then reads "Your dates until the architect confirms them."
Shortlists reclaimed materials and sends them for approval.
Approves materials and requests reservations from the project Approvals and Reservations tabs, and follows them under Your new projects as developer on its Home.

rules: Only a donor building owner can add a New project from Buildings; it is a project, not a building. Add building on its own still opens on Donor building.
The project name must be unique among the owner organisation's projects.
The materials date must be today or later, and site start must leave room for the remaining design stages.
The architect must be an architecture practice. A project has one architect: appointing a second is refused with "This project already has an architect."
The owner may set the programme only while no architect is appointed; after that only the architect can, and keeping or editing makes the dates the architect's plan.
No sustainability consultant is set when the owner creates the project.
On its own projects the owner gets the client workspace: approvals and reservations, not the architect's shortlist tools.

With a New project, the owner Home adds Your new projects as developer: the client dashboard's indicative cost, saving, carbon and reuse tiles, the to do list and the programme, worked out by the same rules.
The owner cannot reserve lots from its own buildings for its own project (see the guard on reserving your own lots).
notifications: The appointed architect: "[owner] added you as architect on [project]. Your client is [owner]."
The project activity log records that the project was created and, later, that the architect was appointed.

workflows.title: Browse the Marketplace as an owner
workflows.where: Marketplace in the owner sidebar (/app/marketplace) and material pages (/app/marketplace/:publicId); also search with Ctrl K or Cmd K
workflows.summary: Every donor building owner may build too, so every owner reads the Marketplace, as a client would: guide prices and the price sort, but nothing to save to. Its own lots never appear there; it manages them in its buildings. A New project is how it checks materials against a start on site.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Marketplace from the sidebar"]:::owner --> B["Own lots left out"]:::system
B --> C{"Has a New project?"}:::system
C -->|"No"| D["Strip offers Add new project"]:::system
D --> E(["New project dialog opens"]):::owner
C -->|"Yes"| F["Check against the New project"]:::owner
F --> G["Cards show fit and guide prices"]:::system
D --> H["Browse, filter, sort by guide price"]:::owner
G --> I(["Open a material page, no Save"]):::owner
H --> I

steps.action: Opens Marketplace, which sits under Home in every owner's sidebar.
Shows the Marketplace in the client view: guide price ranges and the Lowest guide price sort, with no Save to project.
Leaves the owner's own lots out of the grid, the folders, search and material pages.

Without a New project, reads the strip "Building something too? Add a new project to save materials to it and check them against its start on site." and presses Add new project, which opens Buildings on New project.
With a New project, chooses it in the checking strip, so each card shows its fit against that project's materials date.
Opens a material page and reads its facts, availability and guide price, and downloads its drawing, 3D model or BIM model.

rules: Only other sellers' lots show: openly listed ones, lots reserved for the owner's own New projects, and lots shared with them or reached through a share link the owner opened.
An owner never sees its own lots as listings. Opening one of its own material pages shows the no-access page; it manages those lots in its buildings.
Nothing names another seller or building: every card and page is built from the public listing.
Only architects save materials. The architect of the owner's New project shortlists for it; the owner approves and reserves.
New for your projects is for architects only.
Search (Ctrl K or Cmd K) finds other sellers' materials for every owner, never its own.
notifications: None.

workflows.title: Appoint a surveyor to a building
workflows.where: Building, Overview (/app/buildings/:id), Survey card, Surveying firm
workflows.summary: The owner appoints a surveying firm to capture what the building holds, changes the firm, or removes the appointment. The surveyor then captures items and submits the survey.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open building Overview"]:::owner --> B["Pick a firm under Surveying firm"]:::owner
B --> C["Press Save"]:::owner
C --> D{"A surveying firm?"}:::system
D -->|"No"| E(["Refused"]):::system
D -->|"Yes"| F["Appointment recorded"]:::system
F --> G["Surveyor told they are appointed"]:::system
G --> H["Surveyor captures items"]:::surveyor
H --> I["Owner told of each capture"]:::system
I --> J(["Surveyor submits the survey"]):::surveyor

steps.action: Opens the building Overview and, in the Survey card, picks a firm under Surveying firm.
Presses Save. Choosing None and saving removes the appointment.
Records the appointment and tells the firm, which gets the building with Overview, Capture, Inventory, Testing and Requirements tabs.

If the firm had already added the same building itself and captured in it, offers the firm to move those items into this appointment (see Move early captures into an appointment in the surveyor section).
Captures items; each new item is private to the owner and the surveyor.
Submits the survey, and the owner is pointed to the Recovery plan.

rules: Only the building's owner can appoint or remove its surveyor.
The firm must be a surveying or deconstruction firm; anything else is refused with "Choose a surveying firm."
Saving the same firm again changes nothing. A toast offers Undo.
Removing the surveyor takes the building away from that firm; the survey status is kept.
notifications: The surveying firm: "[owner] appointed you to survey [building]", linking to Capture.
The owner: captures are folded into one note, "[person] captured N items at [building]".
The owner, if the firm moves items it captured earlier: "[firm] added N items to [building]", "Captured before your appointment. Private until you decide."
The owner: "[firm] submitted the survey of [building]", linking to the Recovery plan.
Removing the surveyor tells nobody; the building activity log records it.

workflows.title: Confirm or decline a building a surveyor added
workflows.summary: A surveying firm can add a building before any appointment and ask its owner, by email, to confirm it. The owner either confirms it, which brings the building and everything captured into the owner portfolio, confirms it into a building the owner already has with the same surveyor, or says it is not theirs.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Surveyor adds building, names owner email"]:::surveyor --> B["Request waits for that email"]:::system
B --> C["Owner sees it in Requests, Buildings"]:::owner
C --> D{"Is it our building?"}:::owner
D -->|"Yes"| M{"Already ours with this surveyor?"}:::system
M -->|"No"| E["Press Confirm it is ours"]:::owner
E --> F["Building joins donor buildings"]:::system
F --> G(["Surveyor told, stays appointed"]):::system
M -->|"Yes"| N["Press Confirm as your building"]:::owner
N --> O["Items move into the owner record"]:::system
O --> G
D -->|"No"| H["Press Not ours, add optional note"]:::owner
H --> I(["Surveyor told without owner name"]):::system

steps.action: Adds a building to survey and, under Ask the owner to confirm, enters the owner's name, email and a message.
Keeps the request waiting for that email. If an owner account already uses it, that owner is told at once; otherwise it appears once someone signs up with that email as an owner.
Opens Requests, Buildings and sees the building name, address, region, local authority, the firm that added it, how much is captured and the message.

If the owner already has a building that looks like the same place (the same name or address, or the same postcode district with a similar name) with the same surveying firm, warns "You already have [building] with [firm] as surveyor. Confirming adds the surveyor's N items to it, so you keep one record."

Presses Confirm it is ours; or, on a match, Confirm as your [building] or Add as a separate building; or presses Not ours and, in Not your building?, adds an optional Note for the surveyor and confirms with Not ours.

On confirm, makes the owner organisation the building owner and keeps the firm appointed as its surveyor. On Confirm as your [building], moves every item, lot, photo and testing request into the owner's record, fills its gaps (structure, programme and facts), removes the surveyor's copy and lists the request under Answered. On decline, leaves the building with the firm, unlinked.

rules: Only a donor building owner organisation with a member using the email named can answer; others are refused with "This request is addressed to someone else."
A request can be answered once. A building already linked to an owner cannot be claimed again.
Until confirmed, the building is private to the firm, nothing in it can be shared or published, and the survey cannot be submitted.
Confirming adds the building with what was captured; nothing is shared or listed until the owner decides.

Confirm as your [building] is offered only when the owner's matching record has the same surveyor and its survey is not submitted. With a submitted survey the card says the items cannot join it and offers Add as a separate building or Not ours.
Moved items keep their tags unless the owner's building already has items or uses another prefix; then they continue its numbering.
The match is worked out on the owner's side only; the surveyor never learns which buildings the owner has.
On decline the surveyor never learns which organisation answered; the owner's note, if any, is passed on.
Only one request can wait per building. The firm can withdraw it, or ask again after a decline.
Answering marks the owner's notice read for the person who answered. A request that is withdrawn, merged away or deleted takes its notice off the owner's bell.
notifications: Owners using the email, when the request is made: "[firm] surveyed a building for you".
The surveyor on confirm: "[owner] confirmed [building]. You stay appointed as its surveyor."
The surveyor on Confirm as your [building]: "[owner] confirmed [building]. They already had it as [name], so your N items moved there. You stay appointed as its surveyor."
The surveyor on decline: "[building] was not confirmed", with the owner's note or a prompt to check the email, never the owner name.
The Requests item in the owner sidebar shows a count of waiting buildings and reservation requests.
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
state "Waiting for you" as Pending
state "Confirmed" as Accepted
state "Not ours" as Declined
state "Withdrawn" as Withdrawn
[*] --> Pending : surveyor asks the owner
Pending --> Accepted : owner confirms
Pending --> Declined : owner says not ours
Pending --> Withdrawn : surveyor withdraws or deletes
Accepted --> [*]
Declined --> [*]
Withdrawn --> [*]
workflows.states_note: A claim waits for the owner, then ends confirmed, declined or withdrawn. After a decline or withdrawal the surveyor can ask again with a new request.

workflows.title: Read the recovery plan
workflows.summary: Once items are captured, the platform ranks them so the owner can see which are worth taking out carefully and which should go to recycling. The plan is read only; it informs what the owner later lists.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Items captured in the building"]:::surveyor --> B["Platform scores each item out of 100"]:::system
B --> C{"Worth more than removal cost?"}:::system
C -->|"No"| D{"Steel or curtain wall?"}:::system
C -->|"Yes"| E{"Likely to come out intact?"}:::system
E -->|"No"| D
E -->|"Yes"| F["Route: reuse"]:::system
D -->|"Yes"| G["Route: recycle"]:::system
D -->|"No"| H["Route: downcycle"]:::system
F --> I["Owner reviews ranking and totals"]:::owner
G --> I
H --> I
I --> J(["Owner decides what to list"]):::owner

steps.action: Scores every item out of 100 from four parts: net value 40, avoided carbon 30, market demand 20 and ease of removal 10. These weights are placeholders.
Works out net value as the guide price less the cost of careful removal, for the whole quantity.

Marks an item worth recovering (reuse) unless removal would cost more than it fetches or it is unlikely to come out intact; those go to recycle (steel and curtain wall) or downcycle (everything else).
Shows Recoverable net value (indicative), the share Held by the top three, and how many are Worth recovering.
Reads the ranking, highest score first, selects a row to see how its score is made, and checks the UK decision tree legend.
Goes to Listings to decide what to share or publish.

rules: Only the building owner sees the Recovery plan tab; the surveyor and contractor do not.
The UK decision tree has five steps: reuse, upcycle, downcycle, recycle, scrap. This version assigns only reuse, downcycle and recycle.
Figures are indicative and rule based. Nothing on this page changes a lot or what buyers see.
With nothing captured the page shows "Nothing to rank yet".
notifications: None

workflows.title: List a lot: private, shared or published
workflows.where: Building, Listings tab (/app/buildings/:id/listings), List on a private row or Edit on a shared or published one; the same editor appears in the item panel from Inventory
workflows.summary: Each captured item is a lot that starts private. The owner decides whether to keep it private, share it in confidence with selected projects, or publish it to the marketplace, and sets an ask, a reserve and an available-from date.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Listings, press List or Edit"]:::owner --> B{"Lot reserved?"}:::system
B -->|"Yes"| C(["Locked while reserved"]):::system
B -->|"No"| D{"Private, Shared or Published?"}:::owner
D -->|"Private"| E(["Saved as private"]):::system
D -->|"Shared or Published"| F["Enter ask and reserve per unit"]:::owner
F --> G{"Prices valid?"}:::system
G -->|"No"| H(["Fix the prices"]):::owner
G -->|"Yes"| I{"Publishing at a High score?"}:::system
I -->|"Yes"| J(["Blocked, share or disclose less"]):::system
I -->|"No"| K["Press Share, Publish or Save"]:::owner
K --> L(["Matching teams told, owner unnamed"]):::system

steps.action: Opens Listings, filters by All, Private, Shared or Published, and presses List on a private lot or Edit on a shared or published one. The button is greyed out on a reserved lot.
Picks Private, Shared with selected projects, or Published to the marketplace.
For shared or published, enters an Ask and a Reserve per unit, or presses Use suggested.
While the lot is still private, can set Available from; buyers see it as a month or a three-month window.
Shows the disclosure score with this lot and a live preview of the public listing card.
Presses Publish, Share or Save. A toast offers Undo.
Records the change and tells the teams that should know, without naming the owner or the building.

rules: Only the building owner can change a lot. A lot with an accepted reservation is locked: "This lot is reserved. Its visibility cannot change."
Sharing and publishing need an ask and a reserve, both above zero, in whole price steps for the material, with the reserve not above the ask.
Buyers never see the ask or the reserve, only the guide price range.
The available-from date can change only while the lot is private.
Publishing a lot that is not yet published is refused when the disclosure score with it would be High (see the disclosure workflow). Sharing is never blocked by the score.

Private lots are seen only by the owner organisation and its surveyor. Shared lots are seen in confidence by projects the owner allows in Sharing, and by people who open a share link. Published lots are on the marketplace with the building never named.
If the owner makes a lot private while a reservation request is waiting, the request stays open and the owner can still accept it.
notifications: Published: architects whose projects it would reach in time hear "New material for [project]", with no owner or building name.
Shared: the architect and client of each project the owner already allows hear "New lot shared with [project]"; if they have not accepted the confidentiality terms, they are asked to first.
Going private, or changing only the prices, tells nobody; the owner activity log records it.
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
state "Private" as Private
state "Shared with selected projects" as Shared
state "Published to the marketplace" as Published
state "Reserved for a buyer" as Reserved
[*] --> Private : item captured
Private --> Shared
Private --> Published
Shared --> Published
Published --> Shared
Shared --> Private
Published --> Private
Shared --> Reserved : owner accepts a request
Private --> Reserved : owner accepts an earlier request
Published --> Reserved : owner accepts a request
workflows.states_note: A lot moves freely between private, shared and published until the owner accepts a reservation; then it is held for that project and cannot change. A request made while the lot was shared or published can still be accepted after the lot goes private.

workflows.title: Set disclosure and read the disclosure score
workflows.where: Building, Listings tab (/app/buildings/:id/listings), Disclosure settings card; photo switches in the item panel
workflows.summary: The disclosure score estimates how easily an outsider could work out which building the published lots come from. The owner controls how precisely location and timing are shown, and the platform blocks new publishing when the score is High.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Listings, Disclosure settings"]:::owner --> B["Choose location: region or local authority"]:::owner
B --> C["Choose timing: three-month window or month"]:::owner
C --> D["Platform adds up the score"]:::system
D --> E{"Score band?"}:::system
E -->|"Low or Medium"| F(["Publishing allowed"]):::system
E -->|"High"| G["New publishing blocked"]:::system
G --> H["Disclose less, or share instead"]:::owner
H --> D

steps.action: Sets Location shown to Region or Local authority, and Timing shown to Three-month window or Month. Each change saves at once, with Undo.
Chooses, per photo in the item panel, whether it is shown on the listing.

Adds up the score: location 5 for region or 20 for local authority; timing 5 for a window or 15 for a month; published lots 0 for one, 10 for two or three, 20 for four or more; 15 if the published steel includes both beams and columns, or three or more different section sizes; 10 if any public photo.
Bands it Low below 25, Medium from 25, High from 40, and lists in words what an outsider could infer.
Presses Reset to go back to region, three-month window and private photos.

rules: Only the building owner can change disclosure settings or photo visibility.
The score covers the building's published lots only; shared lots do not count.
At High, publishing another lot is refused: "Publishing at this disclosure level lets an outsider narrow down the building. Reduce what is disclosed first." Lots already published stay published.
The score weights and bands are placeholders.
Changing the location or timing setting is never refused, even when it lifts the score to High; only publishing another lot is blocked.
notifications: None

workflows.title: Grant or revoke sharing with projects
workflows.where: Building, Sharing tab (/app/buildings/:id/sharing), Shared with projects list
workflows.summary: The owner chooses which projects on the platform may see the lots it shares in confidence. Each project appears only as a blind line, and the choice applies to every building the owner has.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open the Sharing tab"]:::owner --> B["Read each project as a blind line"]:::owner
B --> C{"Allow this project?"}:::owner
C -->|"No"| E["Switch it off"]:::owner
E --> F(["Project stops seeing shared lots"]):::system
C -->|"Yes"| D["Switch it on"]:::owner
D --> G{"Any lots shared?"}:::system
G -->|"No"| I(["Access recorded"]):::system
G -->|"Yes"| H["Project team told, owner unnamed"]:::system
H --> J{"Terms accepted?"}:::system
J -->|"No"| L["Architect or client accepts terms"]:::arch
J -->|"Yes"| K(["Team sees lots, Shared with you"]):::arch
L --> K

steps.action: Opens Sharing and reads each project as kind of team, project type, region and when materials are needed, never its name.
Turns the switch on or off for a project. A toast offers Undo.
Records the choice for all the owner's buildings and shows Lots shared and Projects allowed.
Accepts the confidentiality terms once for the project, then sees the shared lots in the Marketplace under Shared with you.

rules: Only a donor building owner can grant or revoke. Its own New projects, and any project where it is client or architect, are not listed and are refused.
Which lots are shared is set per lot in Listings; this list decides only which projects may see them.
A project sees shared lots only after its architect or client accepts the confidentiality terms.
Both sides stay anonymous: names are exchanged only when the owner accepts a reservation.
Revoking takes effect at once.
notifications: On granting, when the owner has lots shared: the project's architect and client hear "N lots shared with [project]", shared in confidence by a donor building owner.
Revoking tells nobody; the owner activity log records it as a blind line.

workflows.title: Create, copy and revoke a share link
workflows.where: Building, Sharing tab (/app/buildings/:id/sharing), Share by link card
workflows.summary: The owner can send a link to chosen shared lots of one building to anyone on Tallyard, for example someone outside the projects it already shares with. The owner sees how many organisations opened it, by type only, and can revoke it at any time.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Sharing, Share by link"]:::owner --> B{"Any shared lots?"}:::system
B -->|"No"| C(["Share lots in Listings first"]):::owner
B -->|"Yes"| D["Press Create link"]:::owner
D --> E["Choose shared lots, optional name"]:::owner
E --> F["Link created and copied"]:::system
F --> G["Owner pastes the link to someone"]:::owner
G --> H["Opens counted by organisation type"]:::system
H --> I{"Keep the link?"}:::owner
I -->|"Yes"| J(["Link stays active"]):::system
I -->|"No"| K["Press Revoke, then Revoke link"]:::owner
K --> L(["Openers lose access and are told"]):::system

steps.action: Presses Create link, ticks the shared lots to include (or Select all) and optionally gives it a Name for their own reference.
Creates the link and copies its address; it is listed with its lots, who created it and when.
Uses Copy link to copy it again and Preview to see it as openers do.
Shows "Not opened yet" or, for example, "Opened by 3 organisations (2 architecture practices, 1 developer or client)".
Presses Revoke and confirms Revoke link to withdraw it.

rules: Only the building owner can create or revoke a link.
A link can hold only lots that are shared with selected projects at the time; private, published or reserved lots cannot be added.

If a lot in the link is later made private, it drops out of the link and the row reads, for example, "2 of 3 lots still shared". A lot later published stays in the link. A reserved lot is hidden from people who open the link.
The owner never learns who opened a link, only the type of each organisation. Each organisation counts once.
The name is never shown to people who open the link.
Create link shows only while the building has a shared lot that is not reserved; otherwise the card says Share lots first. Creating a link offers Undo; revoking does not.
Links work only in this browser while the sandbox lasts.
notifications: The owner, on each organisation's first open: "Your share link was opened. An architecture practice opened [name]", folded into a count per link.
Everyone who opened the link, on revoke: "A shared link was withdrawn. Any you saved show as no longer shared."
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
state "Active" as Active
state "Revoked" as Revoked
[*] --> Active : owner creates the link
Active --> Active : an organisation opens it
Active --> Revoked : owner revokes
Revoked --> [*]
workflows.states_note: A link is active from creation until the owner revokes it; a revoked link reads as no longer active for everyone.

workflows.title: What a person who opens a share link sees
who: Anyone signed in (architect, client, consultant, surveyor or another owner)
workflows.summary: Whoever receives a share link opens it while signed in, accepts the confidentiality terms, and then sees the lots as anonymous listings. Their projects can then shortlist and reserve those lots like any other.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Person opens the link, signed in"]:::arch --> Z{"Link made in this sandbox?"}:::system
Z -->|"No"| Y(["This link is not in this sandbox"]):::system
Z -->|"Yes"| B{"Link still active?"}:::system
B -->|"No"| C(["This link is no longer active"]):::system
B -->|"Yes"| D{"Owner organisation itself?"}:::system
D -->|"Yes"| E(["Preview of how others see it"]):::owner
D -->|"No"| F["Shared in confidence terms shown"]:::system
F --> G{"Accept and view?"}:::arch
G -->|"Not now"| H(["Back to home"]):::system
G -->|"Yes"| I["Owner told the organisation type"]:::system
I --> J["Lots shown as anonymous listings"]:::system
J --> K(["Their projects can shortlist and reserve"]):::arch

steps.action: Opens the link while signed in and reads "A donor building owner shared N lots with you".
Presses Accept and view, agreeing not to pass the details on, or Not now.
Records the open for the organisation and tells the owner its type only.
Sees each lot as a card: title, kind of material, quantity, availability window, region or local authority, collection, avoided carbon and sustainability band.
Architects, clients, consultants and owners with a New project open the full material page; architects can save lots to a shortlist. Others open a facts panel.

rules: Openers never see the building name, address, owner, item tag, private photos, ask or reserve.
Terms are accepted once per organisation. The owner organisation itself sees a preview and is never counted as an opener.
Lots made private, and lots reserved by any project, drop out; lots later published stay. With none left the page says "No lots to show".

A revoked link reads "This link is no longer active", and anything saved from it shows as no longer shared. A link this browser has never seen reads "This link is not in this sandbox" and explains that sandbox links open only in the browser where they were made.
Projects where the opener's organisation is architect or client can see the linked lots, without the owner allowing them in Sharing and without the project's own confidentiality terms.
notifications: The owner: "Your share link was opened", with the type of organisation, folded into a count.
The opener, if the owner later revokes: "A shared link was withdrawn".

workflows.title: Accept or decline a reservation request
workflows.where: Requests, Reservations tab (/app/requests), Awaiting you and Decided
workflows.summary: When a client asks to reserve one of the owner's shared or published lots, the owner sees a blind request and accepts or declines it. Accepting holds the lot for that project, declines any competing requests and exchanges names and contacts.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Client asks to reserve a lot"]:::client --> B["Owner told, buyer shown as a blind line"]:::system
B --> C["Owner reviews it in Requests"]:::owner
C --> D{"Accept?"}:::owner
D -->|"No"| E["Press Decline, optional reason"]:::owner
E --> F(["Client told, seller stays unnamed"]):::system
D -->|"Yes"| G["Press Accept, then Accept and reserve"]:::owner
G --> H["Lot held for this project"]:::system
H --> I["Competing requests declined"]:::system
I --> J["Names and contacts exchanged"]:::system
J --> K(["Agree terms directly with the buyer"]):::owner

steps.action: Requests a reservation of an approved material, with a message.
Tells the owner, describing the buyer only as kind of team, project type, region and when it is needed.
Reviews the request with its own indicative figures at the guide price, and a badge if other requests wait for the same lot.
Presses Decline and confirms, with an optional Reason, or presses Accept and confirms Accept and reserve, with an optional Note for the buyer. A toast offers Undo.
On accept, holds the lot for the project, stops offering it, declines other waiting requests with "Reserved for another buyer", and shows each side the other's organisation, contact and email.
Agrees the terms directly with the buyer, outside the platform.

rules: Only the owner of the lot's building can decide. A request can be decided once.
Only one request per lot can be accepted; accepting when another is already accepted is refused with "Reserved for another buyer."
Before acceptance neither side learns who the other is. After it, the owner sees the buyer's organisation, contact, email and message, and the client sees the seller's.
The architect and the consultant never see who the seller is.
A reserved lot is locked: its visibility, prices and date cannot change and it cannot go in a share link.
The client can withdraw a request while it waits; it then leaves the owner's list. Decided keeps accepted and declined requests only.
Before acceptance the owner does not see the buyer's message; the screen says it is shared when the owner accepts.
notifications: The owner, on a new request: "Reservation request for [tag]" with the blind buyer line; on withdrawal: "Request withdrawn for [tag]".
The client, on accept: "[seller] accepted your reservation" with the seller contact and email. Any note for the buyer shows on the client's Reservations tab as the seller's note.
The architect, on accept: "[material] is reserved", without the seller name.
The client, on decline: "Reservation declined: [material]", with "The seller's note: [reason]" or "The seller declined this request."
Clients of competing requests: "Reservation declined: [material]", with "Reserved for another buyer."
On a decline the architect and consultant are not notified; their project activity shows that the seller declined.
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
state "Awaiting your decision" as Pending
state "Reserved" as Accepted
state "Declined" as Declined
state "Withdrawn" as Withdrawn
[*] --> Pending : client requests
Pending --> Accepted : owner accepts
Pending --> Declined : owner declines
Pending --> Declined : another request accepted
Pending --> Withdrawn : client withdraws
Accepted --> [*]
Declined --> [*]
Withdrawn --> [*]
workflows.states_note: A request waits for the owner, then ends reserved, declined (by the owner or because another buyer was accepted) or withdrawn by the client.

workflows.title: Request testing of items
workflows.where: Building, Testing tab (/app/buildings/:id/testing), button Request testing
workflows.summary: The owner, or the surveyor, asks one of the listed testing companies to inspect or test chosen items, with a preferred date and a message, then records the visit and the results. Either side can view, copy or download the request sheet the company would receive. Results update each item's test status, and steel grade, which buyers see on listings.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Testing, press Request testing"]:::owner --> B["Choose the items"]:::owner
B --> C["Choose tests that suit them"]:::owner
C --> D["Choose a company, date and message"]:::owner
D --> E["Press Send request"]:::owner
E --> F["Recorded, other side told"]:::system
F --> V["View request: copy or download"]:::owner
V --> G{"Visit going ahead?"}:::owner
G -->|"No"| H(["Press Cancel"]):::owner
G -->|"Yes"| I["Record booking with visit date"]:::owner
I --> J["Record results, one per item"]:::owner
J --> K(["Test status shows on listings"]):::system

steps.action: Presses Request testing, ticks the items, then the tests offered for those kinds of item.
Picks a Company that offers every chosen test in the building's region, optionally a Preferred from date and a Message, and presses Send request.

Records the request as Sent and tells the surveyor. The card shows Preferred from [date] and the message. Nothing is sent to the company in the sandbox; the confirmation names who was told, points to View request and offers Undo.

Presses View request to open "Request to [company]": the sheet the company would receive, with who it is to and from, the building, each item with its size, quantity and location, the tests, the preferred date and the message; presses Copy text or Download .txt.
Presses Record booking and saves the visit date the company confirmed; Change booking moves it.
Presses Record results and saves one result per item, with a steel grade where a grade test was done.
Can instead press Cancel and confirm Cancel request, with an optional reason, until results are recorded.
Updates each item's test status and grade, which show on any listing.

rules: Only the owner or the appointed surveyor can request, book, record or cancel; a contractor alone cannot.
At least one item and one test are needed; the company must offer every chosen test in the region.
The preferred date and the visit date must be today or later. With no preferred date the sheet reads "Preferred from: no preference".
The request sheet is marked Simulated: "A sample request. No testing company receives it." Both sides can view it on every request, whatever its status.
Results need one line per item. Items whose lots are reserved cannot change.
Only the owner records results for items that are shared or published, as only the owner changes what a listing says.
A request can be cancelled only before results are recorded.
notifications: The surveyor, when the owner acts (or the owner, when the surveyor acts): "[person] asked [company] to test N items", "Testing visit booked", "Test results recorded".
Cancelling tells nobody; the building activity log records it.
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
state "Sent" as Requested
state "Visit booked" as Booked
state "Results recorded" as Results
state "Cancelled" as Cancelled
[*] --> Requested : request sent
Requested --> Booked : booking recorded
Booked --> Booked : booking changed
Booked --> Results : results recorded
Requested --> Cancelled
Booked --> Cancelled
Results --> [*]
Cancelled --> [*]
workflows.states_note: A testing request is sent, then booked, then has results; it can be cancelled until results are in.

workflows.title: Appoint a contractor and apply their dates
workflows.where: Building, Overview (/app/buildings/:id), Deconstruction contractor card; then Inventory (/app/buildings/:id/inventory)
workflows.summary: The owner invites a deconstruction contractor to say when each item is expected to come out, choosing a firm already on Tallyard or inviting one by email. A new contractor never inherits the previous one's dates. The contractor's dates stay apart from what buyers see until the owner applies them to private lots.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open Overview, contractor card"]:::owner --> B{"Firm in the list?"}:::owner
B -->|"Yes"| C["Choose the firm, press Save"]:::owner
B -->|"No"| D["Invite by email, Send invite"]:::owner
D --> E{"Firm on Tallyard with that email?"}:::system
E -->|"Yes"| C2["Firm appointed at once"]:::system
E -->|"No"| W["Invite waits on the building"]:::system
W --> J["Firm joins with that email"]:::contractor
C --> X["Previous contractor's dates cleared"]:::system
C2 --> X
J --> X
X --> T["Contractor told to set dates"]:::system
T --> S["Contractor sets a month per item"]:::contractor
S --> U["Owner compares, Use contractor dates"]:::owner
U --> V{"Lot private and not reserved?"}:::system
V -->|"Yes"| Y(["Lot date updated"]):::system
V -->|"No"| Z(["Skipped, make private to change"]):::system

steps.action: In the Deconstruction contractor card, picks a firm under Invite a contractor (or Change contractor) and presses Save. Choosing None removes it.
For a firm not in the list, presses Invite by email, enters the Contractor's email and presses Send invite.

If a surveying or deconstruction firm on Tallyard uses that email, appoints it at once and names it. Otherwise the card shows Invited, Waiting for [email], with Withdraw, and the firm becomes the contractor when it signs up as a surveying or deconstruction firm, or joins one by invite, with that email.

When the contractor changes or is removed, clears every date the previous contractor set and says so, for example "Fennick Dismantling's 5 dates were cleared."; Undo restores them. A waiting invite says the dates are cleared when the new firm joins.
Tells the firm, which gets the building with only Overview and Availability tabs.
On Availability, sets or clears the month each item is expected to come out.
Stores each date as the dismantling start if it falls in that month, otherwise the first of the month, and tells the owner.
Sees the contractor date beside each lot in Inventory, and presses Use contractor dates (N) for all, or Use contractor date in one item panel.
Updates private, unreserved lots and reports how many were skipped because they are shared, published or reserved.

rules: The owner or the surveyor can invite, change or remove a contractor. A firm chosen from the list must be a surveying or deconstruction firm.

An invite by email never reveals who is on Tallyard: an email at an organisation of another kind is treated like an unknown one and simply waits. Only a surveying or deconstruction firm joining with that email takes it up.
One invite waits per building. Choosing a firm from the list replaces it, and Withdraw cancels it. Nothing is emailed from the sandbox.
A new contractor never inherits the previous contractor's dates.
Only the appointed contractor can set these dates. A contractor never sees lots, prices or buyers, and cannot capture, test or open the building's requirements.
Contractor dates never reach buyers directly; only the owner changes a lot's date, and only while the lot is private.
A firm that is also the surveyor gets the Availability tab beside its other tabs.
notifications: The contractor: "[owner] invited you to set availability dates at [building]", also when it joins from an email invite.
When a firm joins from an email invite, the side that invited it and the owner: "[firm] joined and can set dates at [building]", with "They accepted your invitation." and any dates that were cleared.
The owner: "[contractor] set dates for N items at [building]. Review them in the inventory and apply the ones you agree with", folded per day.
The owner, if the surveyor invited the contractor: "[surveyor] invited [contractor] to [building]".
Removing the contractor, or recording or withdrawing an invite by email, tells nobody; the building activity log records it.

workflows.title: Track requirements before demolition
workflows.where: Building, Requirements tab (/app/buildings/:id/requirements); the Requirements line on the owner Home building card and on the surveyor Home building row
workflows.summary: Each donor building tracks the planning requirements that apply before it comes down at its location: a national demolition notice, in London the pre-demolition audit and diversion target, and the local authority's own policy. The owner and the surveyor keep each one's status and evidence current.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Open the building's Requirements tab"]:::owner --> B["What applies at this place listed"]:::system
B --> C{"What needs updating?"}:::owner
C -->|"Status"| D["Choose a status"]:::owner
C -->|"Evidence"| E["Add a note of evidence"]:::owner
E --> F["Not started becomes In progress"]:::system
D --> G{"Surveyor marked at risk or ready?"}:::system
G -->|"Yes"| H["Owner is notified"]:::system
G -->|"No"| I(["Saved and logged"]):::system
H --> I
F --> I
I --> J(["At risk counted on homes and the tab"]):::system

steps.action: Picks the requirements from the building's region and local authority: National (England, Wales or Scotland, before demolition), the London Plan 2021 and GLA guidance for a London region, and the local authority's plan when one is set. An authority with no written summary gets a placeholder marked Not yet summarised.
Opens the Requirements tab from the building or the sidebar, or follows the line on the owner's building card or the surveyor's building row, for example "Requirements 1 of 4 ready, 1 at risk".
Sets a status: Not started, In progress, At risk, Evidence ready or Not applicable.
Adds evidence as a note; the first evidence moves a Not started requirement to In progress.
Logs each change in the building activity for the owner and the surveyor, and counts the requirements at risk as a badge on the tab and its sidebar item.

When moving the building to another region or local authority in Edit details, reads how many requirements stop applying and how many more are tracked; statuses and evidence stay with the ones that still apply.

rules: Only the owner and the surveyor of the building can open the tab and change it. A firm that is only the deconstruction contractor cannot open it, nor can any buyer.
Requirement activity reaches the owner and the surveyor only, never the contractor. A firm that both surveys and dismantles hears as the surveyor.
Only the person who added a piece of evidence can remove it. Each change offers Undo.
Not applicable requirements are left out of the total and the ready share.
Every entry is an indicative summary to check against the published documents; a placeholder summarises nothing yet.
Nothing on this tab reaches a listing or a buyer.
notifications: The owner, when the surveyor marks a requirement At risk or Evidence ready: "[requirement] is [status] on [building]", "Marked by [name], [firm]."
Every other change, and every change the owner makes: no notification, an entry in the building activity only.

workflows.title: The guard on reserving your own lots
who: Donor building owner (as client of a New project)
workflows.summary: An owner that is also the client of a New project may come across its own lots, for example published ones its architect shortlists. The platform refuses a reservation of a lot from the owner's own building, because reserving is for buying from other sellers.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Architect shortlists a lot"]:::arch --> B["Owner approves it"]:::owner
B --> C["Owner presses Request reservation"]:::owner
C --> D["Owner presses Send request"]:::owner
D --> E{"Lot from the owner's own building?"}:::system
E -->|"Yes"| F(["Refused: this lot is yours"]):::system
E -->|"No"| G["Request sent to the seller"]:::system
G --> H(["Seller accepts or declines"]):::owner

steps.action: Shortlists a material for the New project and sends it for approval.
Approves it on the Approvals tab, then on Reservations presses Request reservation and Send request.
Checks who owns the lot's building. If it is the project's own client, refuses with "This lot is yours. Allocate it directly; reserving is for other sellers."
Otherwise sends a blind request to the seller, as for any client.

rules: A New project cannot reserve a lot from a building its own client owns.
Nothing stops the architect shortlisting, or the owner approving, its own lots; the refusal comes only at Send request.

The owner never sees its own lots in the Marketplace, search or as material pages, but its architect can. The owner cannot allow its own projects in Sharing, and opening its own share link does not count. Its shared lots still reach its New project if that project's architect opens one of the owner's share links; published lots always do.
Allocating your own materials directly is not in this version.
notifications: None; the refusal is shown on screen.
